summary: The BYD Seal is a fast-charging, long-range electric sedan that undercuts the Tesla Model 3 on price while matching it on performance, especially in dual-motor Performance guise. Australian reviewers rate the equipment list, warranty and everyday value highly, but consistently flag a boot smaller than key rivals, an unsettled ride on rougher roads, and a touchscreen-heavy interior with few physical controls. BYD dropped the entry-level Dynamic in June 2026 after slow sales, so the range is now just the rear-drive Premium and the dual-motor Performance.
pros: Strong value against the Tesla Model 3, with a well-equipped cabin and quick acceleration in Performance guise (390kW/670Nm, 0-100km/h in 3.8s)
Long WLTP range from the 82.56kWh Blade LFP battery: 570km (Premium) and 520km (Performance), with 150kW DC fast charging
Strong after-sales backing with a 6-year/150,000km vehicle warranty and 8-year/160,000km battery warranty
cons: 400L boot trails key rivals like the Tesla Model 3 (594L) and Toyota Camry (524L), with a narrow opening
Ride quality criticised as unsettled and bouncy over bumps, lacking the composure of segment rivals
Interior tech feels dated relative to newer BYD models, with too many functions buried in touchscreen menus rather than physical controls
Prices were cut by $2,808-$3,758 in January 2025 (Premium from $55,798, Performance from $65,748), hitting the resale value of earlier cars despite BYD's distributor vowing in 2023 not to discount
